newsitem.title: USA: Westinghouse shares seen spurred by plan.
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse shares seen spurred by plan.

text.p: Ending months of waiting on Wall Street, Westinghouse Electric Corp early Wednesday announced its plan to split into two companies and early reviews show the time was well spent.
"It looks like a very well thought out plan," said Nicholas Heymann, an analyst at NatWest Securities. "This should move the stock comfortably through 21 today."
Shares in Westinghouse, which have rallied in anticipation of the plan from just above 17 at the start of the month to 20-5/8 on Tuesday, added 1/4 to 20-7/8 in pre-open activity, traders said.

Heymann said the plan, which involves splitting Westinghouse's media and industrial businesses and an initial public offering of 20 percent of the industrial company's transportation refrigeration unit Thermo King, included "a few positive surprises, a few creative things."
The Thermo King offering, he said, "will insure the industrial spin-off is exceptionally strong financial condition."
And although the media company will assume Westinghouse's debt obligations, it also gains custody of the conglomerate's net operating loss carryforwards, a key tax benefit.

Heymann said the plan settled nearly all the important questions about the future of Westinghouse, with the sole major exception being who would assume leadership of the industrial spin-off, to be called WELCO.
However, Heymann said he was not concerned about that issue. "I think there will be very well known outsider brought in to run the industrial company," he said.
The media company will be headed by Westinghouse's current chairman Michael Jordan.
